note: France keeps no private bureau's record but the Banque de France's file of repayment incidents (FICP). A monthly credit is listed once arrears equal the last two installments due, and only after the lender's warning gives 30 days to settle: the second installment falls about 30 days after the first, written as 60 days from the first due date. The listing lasts five years at most, struck off early once settled. On 2026-11-03 the Banque de France's FICP page refused this environment (Akamai's 'Access Denied', to curl and to a rendering browser alike; Légifrance's text of the FICP's arrêté answered with a Cloudflare check, and archive.org didn't answer); Common Crawl's copy of the page of 8 September 2026 was read instead and still says what is quoted, so the page keeps its reading of 2026-10-30.

sources.title: Banque de France, Que signifie être fiché au FICP ?
sources.said: a accumulé, pour un crédit remboursable mensuellement, un retard de paiement égal au montant des deux dernières échéances dues ; ... Vous disposez alors de 30 jours pour régulariser. A défaut, l’établissement procèdera à votre inscription au FICP. ... La durée d’inscription est alors de cinq ans maximum.
